snippet.title: Iran Blows Up 'U.S.-Navy Guided Ships' In Hormuz; 4 Million Barrel Crude Vessels Hit Naval Mines
snippet.description:
Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz have escalated again, with Iran claiming that two oil tankers caught fire after striking naval mines while transiting the strategic waterway. Iranian state media said the vessels were carrying around 2 million barrels of crude oil and accused them of switching off their positioning and radar systems before attempting to use a route Tehran had not authorised. The incidents come amid escalating attacks on commercial shipping and a US blockade of Iranian ports. The conflict has disrupted energy flows through the strait, a critical global shipping route responsible for a significant share of worldwide energy supplies. According to Kpler figures, oil flows through Hormuz averaged 11.6 million barrels per day in the seven days to October 13, around 68% of the pre-war baseline. Meanwhile, US Central Command chief Brad Cooper said 400 ships and 100 million barrels of oil had moved through the strait over the past week despite Iranian attacks.

snippet.title: Landmarks fall after student protests rage across France
snippet.description:
France burns as protests reach 'worst unrest in years'

#france #protest #paris #world #breakingnews

Read more ► [http://news.com.au/c99e276932ef1f5fcae9d429cda3f256/ ]

Violent clashes have broken out across France as more than half a million people took to the streets to protest the rising cost of living, with one demonstrator’s hand blown off, multiple blazes set and looters breaking into dozens of stores to strip them bare.

In Paris, tens of thousands marched across the east and north of the city in one major march, some shouting “Everyone hates the police” and “Macron, resign”.

“To those who clearly want to use this violence as a ‘warm-up’ before the presidential election, I say clearly: We will not let ourselves be intimidated. No one will impose their political agenda through violence,” France’s Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu wrote on social media.

An estimated 500,000 people turned out at 1,750 rallies across the country on Saturday, according to France’s main CGT union.

“The government must stop its repression and respond immediately to the social demands,” it said in a statement, after police fired tear gas, crowd-control grenades and water canons at protesters, some of whom clashed with security forced their way into public buildings.

localized.title: Landmarks fall after student protests rage across France
localized.description:
France burns as protests reach 'worst unrest in years'

#france #protest #paris #world #breakingnews

Read more ► [http://news.com.au/c99e276932ef1f5fcae9d429cda3f256/ ]

Violent clashes have broken out across France as more than half a million people took to the streets to protest the rising cost of living, with one demonstrator’s hand blown off, multiple blazes set and looters breaking into dozens of stores to strip them bare.

In Paris, tens of thousands marched across the east and north of the city in one major march, some shouting “Everyone hates the police” and “Macron, resign”.

“To those who clearly want to use this violence as a ‘warm-up’ before the presidential election, I say clearly: We will not let ourselves be intimidated. No one will impose their political agenda through violence,” France’s Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu wrote on social media.

An estimated 500,000 people turned out at 1,750 rallies across the country on Saturday, according to France’s main CGT union.

“The government must stop its repression and respond immediately to the social demands,” it said in a statement, after police fired tear gas, crowd-control grenades and water canons at protesters, some of whom clashed with security forced their way into public buildings.

snippet.description:

Jacinto trabajó durante 12 años limpiando una fábrica de pan. Nadie valoraba sus conocimientos porque no tenía estudios técnicos, pero una noche logró reparar un horno industrial que llevaba días sin funcionar. En lugar de agradecerle, sus superiores decidieron despedirlo.

Lo que nadie imaginaba era que aquella injusticia cambiaría su destino. Un empresario descubrió su verdadero talento y le ofreció la oportunidad de demostrar de qué era capaz.
